ara: quick heads-up, ran a multi-model co-residency pass this morning (model-A small, model-B medium, model-C large). saw a perf regression vs yesterday on 1xA100. 
ara: timeline: after warmup KV-cache refill spikes, allocator churns, then OOM on swap path. curious if kernel selector change could be the trigger. :thinking:
cheng: can you paste the nvprof/trace? rough numbers enough for now
ara: pasted snapshot from profiler and allocator trace below:
ara: ```
# top hotspots (samples)
attention_kernel_v2_fused  41.9%
memcpy_htod_async         18.3%
alloc_gpu_workspace      12.7%
kv_cache_restore         9.8%
others                   17.3%
# peak mem: expected 8.2GB, observed peak 10.8GB
# OOM log: allocate(672MB) failed, free_pool=120MB, active_kv=2.6GB
```
marta: thanks. couple hypotheses: 1) kernel selector chose int8-fused attention for model-B which increases transient workspace by ~1.5x for certain seq_len + batch combos; 2) KV cache restore is doing synchronous memcpy on main path causing allocator fragmentation; 3) we regressed batching heuristics so more micro-batches hit the same alloc pattern.
lucas: +1 on workspace impact. fused kernels often trade compute for extra temp buffers. if selector ignores "workspace" metric it can pick faster kernel that blows VRAM. we added that metric last month but maybe flag flipped in rollout? :eyes:
cheng: I remember a toggle landed: KERNEL_PRIORITIZE_LATENCY=true by default. would cause that. can we repro with KERNEL_DEBUG_SCOREBOARD=1 and dump candidate scores?
ara: repro script: ```bash
# repro harness (dev GPU)
python tools/repro_multi_model.py --models A,B,C --seq-lens 32,512 --batch 4 --trace nvtx --env KERNEL_PRIORITIZE_LATENCY=1
```
ara: initial quick fix idea: policy to bias kernel selection when free_vram < threshold: prefer "mem-light" kernels even if slightly slower. also adaptive batching: shrink micro-batches before starting KV restore.
marta: also need allocator-level fixes: tune free-list bucket sizes and enable buffer reuse between attention and feedforward temporaries. current allocator creates many small chunks on kv restore, causing fragmentation. propose enabling delayed_free_coalesce and increase min_chunk_size to 8KB for next week A/B.
lucas: for co-residency isolation: we could reserve per-model workspace slabs at allocation time (zoning) so single model's transient can't steal others. downside is potential wasted capacity. tradeoff ok for SLA-critical customers.
cheng: can we do hybrid: soft-reserve (try to keep slab) + evictable tags for lower tier models. eviction policy: prefer KV segments older than X requests, then model-swap.
ara: ops-bot: deploy candidate kernel-selector patch to staging?
ops-bot: deploy triggered by ara. build 2026.03.18-ker-sel-avoid-mem queued.
lucas: experiment suggestion: run A/B across 10 hosts: control=master, variant=mem-aware kernel select + delayed_coalesce. metrics: p99 latency, peak_vram, OOM_count, effective_throughput. also add allocation timeline tracing (TRACK_ALLOC=1).
marta: added quick profiler diff in thread: ```
# before (master)
peak 10.8GB, allocs 324, avg_alloc 28MB
# after (mem-aware)
peak 8.9GB, allocs 268, avg_alloc 32MB
# notes: fewer tiny allocs, more reuse. p99 latency +2% for model-B, throughput unchanged
```
cheng: ok this looks promising. next steps: 1) revert KERNEL_PRIORITIZE_LATENCY flip in canary while we validate; 2) roll allocator param change as runtime config; 3) add adaptive batching hook to front of request pipeline to shrink batches when free_vram < margin. who can own?
ara: I can take adaptive batching prototype (small change in router: if free_vram < target_margin -> reduce batch cap by 25%).
marta: I will own allocator params and buffer-reuse patch. will run leak/tracing job and post heap timeline by EOD.
lucas: I'll own kernel-selector scoreboard dump + add workspace metric into candidate scoring.
cheng: I'll coordinate canary toggles and A/B measurement.
ara: cool. let's sync tomorrow 10am to review A/B results. tagging @here for visibility. :thumbsup:
